bug_description.original: A crash occurs when the hash function is called with zero-length buffers, as it does not handle empty strings.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 52-byte ASS witness ends with a `Dialogue` text field `{\fn@}`. `process_event_tail()` duplicates that field into a 7-byte heap buffer, `parse_tags()` stores the `\fn` argument as a one-byte family view `@`, and `update_font()` treats that lone `@` as the vertical-font prefix, increments the pointer to the closing brace, and decrements the length to zero. Font-cache hashing then reaches `fnv_32a_buf()` with a pointer into that heap string and `len == 0`; because the vulnerable helper lacks the later `if (!len) return hval;` guard, its `case 0: do { ... }` body still executes once and the fallthrough read at `libass/ass_utils.h:194` runs past the 7-byte `event->Text` allocation, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `fnv_32a_buf -> font_hash -> ass_cache_get`.

source.description: Source. `process_event_tail()` first materializes the attacker-controlled `Text` field as heap string `event->Text`. For the witness this duplicates the exact event text `{\fn@}`, creating the 7-byte allocation that later holds the `\fn` argument and is over-read at the sink.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is 52 bytes with sha256 `e81bddf09925e87c8739d46cefedeecedacaa7c90f43c4713558473fb2e259f1` and ends with `Dialogue:,,2:3:0.0,,,,,,,{\fn@}`. By the time `process_event_tail()` reaches the `Text` column, `p` points at the 6-byte event text `{\fn@}`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After `fnv_32a_buf()` has already consumed the `}` byte and the terminating NUL from the 7-byte `event->Text` allocation, the next fallthrough `*bp++` at line 194 reaches the first heap-redzone byte just past that allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address ... READ of size 1` at `fnv_32a_buf /src/libass/libass/./ass_utils.h:194:26` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 7-byte region allocated by `process_event_tail()`.

root_cause.code: switch (len % 4) { case 0: do { hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; //-fallthrough case 3:      hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; //-fallthrough case 2:      hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; //-fallthrough case 1:      hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; } while (--n > 0); }
root_cause.description: Root cause. `fnv_32a_buf()` reaches this `switch` even when `len == 0`. Because the vulnerable source has no early `if (!len) return hval;` guard, `len % 4 == 0` selects `case 0` and the `do { ... } while (--n > 0)` body executes once despite `n` having been computed as 0.
root_cause.note: The fix commit inserts exactly that missing zero-length return ahead of this code. Without it, a zero-length family view still causes the hash helper to dereference `bp`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the vulnerability-relevant zero-length hash input is created. The one-byte family override `@` is interpreted as a vertical-font marker, so `update_font()` advances the pointer to the closing `}` inside `event->Text` and decrements the length from 1 to 0.

parser_admitted.description: Once the witness has entered the `[events]` section and the line begins with `Dialogue:`, libass allocates an event and dispatches the remaining CSV tail to `process_event_tail()`. The PoC's `Text` field therefore enters the normal ASS event parser instead of being rejected as malformed input.

coarse_trace.summary: The ASS event parser accepts the `Dialogue:` line and duplicates its `Text` field `{\fn@}` into heap string `event->Text`.

The `\fn` tag parser stores a one-byte family view `@`, and `update_font()` immediately strips that sole vertical-font marker, leaving `desc.family.len == 0` while the pointer now aliases the closing `}` byte inside `event->Text`.
Font lookup hashes the descriptor before probing the cache, so the zero-length `desc.family` reaches `fnv_32a_buf()` as the family component of the font-cache key.
The vulnerable hash helper computes `n == 0` from `len == 0` but still enters its `case 0: do { ... }` body once, and the fallthrough reads walk off the 7-byte `event->Text` allocation at line 194.

fine_trace.note: Materializes the attacker-controlled `Text` field as heap string `event->Text`. For the witness, `p` is `{\fn@}`, so this allocation is 7 bytes long including the trailing NUL; ASan later names this `strdup` as the allocation context for the over-read region.

fine_trace.code: if (nargs && strncmp(start, "0", args->end - start)) { skip_spaces(&start); render_priv->state.family.str = start; render_priv->state.family.len = args->end - start; }
fine_trace.note: When parsing `\fn@`, `nargs` is 1 and `strncmp("@", "0", 1)` is nonzero, so the override branch stores a StringView into `event->Text`: `start` points at the lone `@` byte and `args->end - start` is 1 because `args->end` is the closing `}`.

fine_trace.code: desc.family = render_priv->state.family; if (desc.family.len && desc.family.str[0] == '@') { desc.vertical = 1; desc.family.str++; desc.family.len--; }
fine_trace.note: The one-byte family view from step 2 satisfies the vertical-font check, so `update_font()` strips the only `@`. That leaves `desc.family.len == 0` and advances `desc.family.str` from the `@` byte to the closing `}` byte inside the 7-byte `event->Text` allocation.

During font-cache hashing (`ass_font_new -> ass_cache_get -> font_hash`), the zero-length family from step 3 reaches `fnv_32a_buf()` as `(buf, len)`. The helper aliases that pointer as `bp`, and `len == 0` yields `n == 0`; `bp` still points at the closing `}` byte near the end of the heap string from step 1.

fine_trace.code: switch (len % 4) { case 0: do { hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; //-fallthrough case 3:      hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; //-fallthrough case 2:      hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; //-fallthrough case 1:      hval ^= *bp++; hval *= FNV1_32A_PRIME; } while (--n > 0); }
fine_trace.note: Root cause step. The vulnerable helper does not return early for `len == 0`, so `len % 4 == 0` still enters `case 0`. Because this is a `do ... while`, the body executes once even though step 4 computed `n == 0`, forcing at least one dereference of `bp` for a logically empty buffer.

Sink. Starting from the `}` byte selected in step 3, the fallthrough body first consumes `}` and the terminating NUL from the 7-byte `event->Text` buffer. The next `*bp++` read reported at line 194 reaches the first byte past that allocation, producing the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ 1`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of a 7-byte heap region allocated by `strdup` here.

format.name: ASS subtitle
format.contract: The witness must parse as an ASS subtitle with an `[events]` section and a `Dialogue:` line whose `Text` field is exactly `{\fn@}` so the entire `\fn` argument is the lone `@` byte. `update_font()` must then strip that vertical-font marker, leaving `len == 0` before the font-cache hash call.
